item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 240526
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located a few hundred miles
south-southwest of Hilo, Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Iselle,
located several hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to form well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands during the middle part of the
week. Some slow development of this system is possible later this
week while it moves northeastward or northward across the western
portion of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ34 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 33.3 North, longitude 174.8 West. Lala is
moving toward the north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A slow 
northwestward motion is forecast during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 47
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 240232
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  47
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Lala remains a well organized tropical storm despite moving over 
cool waters. The system is maintaining a partial eyewall that wraps 
a little more than halfway around the center, along with 
numerous fragmented outer rainbands. There has been little change in 
the latest satellite intensity estimates, and a blend of the latest 
objective and subjective estimates supports holding the initial 
intensity steady at 55 kt. An ASCAT-C pass from around 21Z was 
helpful in adjusting the 34- and 50-kt wind radii.

The storm is moving slowly northwestward at about 6 kt. An even 
slower northwestward motion is expected during the next few days as 
Lala is forecast to remain located just southwest of a strong 
subtropical ridge, not far from the ridge axis where the steering 
currents are weak. This motion should cause Lala to cross the 
International Date Line around the middle of the week. Although the 
models show the same general theme, there is a fair amount of 
cross-track spread beyond 72 hours. The NHC track forecast is 
similar to the previous one and lies closer to the left side of the 
guidance envelope, near the Google DeepMind, HCCA, and TVCA aids.

Lala is expected to weaken over the next several days as it moves 
over progressively cooler waters, but the weakening trend will 
likely be slow since it is expected to remain in generally low wind 
shear conditions. The GFS and ECMWF models show the storm losing 
organized deep convection around the time it nears the International 
Date Line in a few days. Based on that guidance, the transition to a 
post-tropical cyclone has been moved up to day 4.  Otherwise, this 
intensity forecast is very similar to the previous one and near the 
middle of the guidance envelope.

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA33 PHFO 240849
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Moke Advisory Number  16
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
...HEAVY RAIN AND GUSTY WINDS SPREADING ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE BIG
ISLAND OF HAWAII AND MAUI...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.3N 158.6W
ABOUT 380 MI...615 KM SW OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke 
was located near latitude 15.3 North, longitude 158.6 West. The 
depression is moving toward the west near 13 mph (20 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue during the next day or two. 
On the forecast track, the center of Moke will pass southwest of the 
Big Island of Hawaii overnight and well south of the smaller main 
Hawaiian Islands on Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected, and Moke is forecast to degenerate to a
remnant low pressure area by late Monday and dissipate on Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
NOAA buoy 51002 to the north-northeast of Moke recently reported a
sustained wind of 31 mph (50 km/h) and a gust of 36 mph (58 km/h).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Depression Moke can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO
header WTPA43 PHFO.
 
WIND: Gusty winds are likely across the Hawaiian Islands during the
next day or two, especially in areas of high terrain.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Depression Moke is expected to produce additional
rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches through Monday across the Big
Island. Rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches of rain are expected on
eastern Maui. These rainfall amounts may produce life-threatening
flooding and mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island,
especially in steep terrain and over areas that were affected
recently by Lala.
 
Across western Maui and the remainder of the islands, Tropical
Depression Moke may produce up to 1 or 2 inches of rain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
632 
WTPA43 PHFO 240850
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  16
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Proxy-visible satellite images of Moke show the low-level center 
remains exposed tonight. The depression has only produced small, 
intermittent bursts of convection over the northern part of its 
circulation during the past several hours. Although Moke is centered 
well to the south of the Hawaiian Islands, NWS radar data and 
surface observations indicate that heavy rain and gusty winds are 
spreading across portions of the Big Island of Hawaii and Maui. 
Based on earlier scatterometer data and given no recent improvements 
to the satellite presentation of Moke, the initial intensity is held 
at 30 kt.
 
The depression is moving westward (275/11 kt) and should continue on
this heading for the next couple of days while being steered by a
strong low- to mid-level ridge to its north. No notable changes were
made to the NHC track forecast, which keeps the center of Moke well
south of the main Hawaiian Islands. Regardless, periods of heavy
rain and gusty winds are expected across portions of the islands
overnight through Monday.
 
Moke may not remain a tropical cyclone for much longer if it is
unable to generate more organized convection soon. Persistent
southwesterly shear and the drier surrounding mid-level environment
suggest this is unlikely to occur. Based on recent satellite trends
and the latest global model wind fields and simulated satellite
images, the updated NHC forecast now shows Moke becoming a
post-tropical remnant low in 24 h and dissipating by 48 h. Note that
this could occur even sooner than forecast.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rain bands associated with Tropical Depression Moke will continue
over the Big Island while spreading westward across the remainder of
the Hawaiian Islands through Monday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides for the windward and
southeast Big Island, especially in steep terrain and over areas
that were affected recently by Lala.
 
2. Strong, gusty winds are likely as Moke passes south of the main
Hawaiian Islands, particularly in areas within and downslope of
higher terrain.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  24/0900Z 15.3N 158.6W   30 KT  35 MPH
